title: AP Computer Science A

rows.task: Review the Chapter 1 work already assigned: Eclipse setup, Part A/B videos, prequizzes and Lab Exercise 5.
rows.evidence: Existing Chapter 1 work; no new retrospective submission.
rows.homework: As already assigned: Chapter 1 Part A/B prequizzes and Lab Exercise 5 for Sep 9.

rows.task: Check the Hello.java error experiments, then take the already-posted nine-question quiz. Debrief syntax versus output errors and preview integer division.
rows.evidence: Existing Lab 5 file/answers; nine-question quiz; one corrected error explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: preview L02 Two Meanings of Plus; predict each output before compiling.

rows.task: Repair average, wholePart and remainder in ExpressionLab. Use Circle as a short transfer on constants, assignment and numeric output. Read one keyboard value with Scanner.
rows.evidence: ExpressionLab checks; value/type table; explain why double x = 7/2 loses the fraction.
rows.homework: 20 min: L04 Painting a Room calculation and two expected outputs; finish any ExpressionLab repair.

rows.task: Read the API and method contracts. Complete scaleSample and roll; test samples 0 and just below 1, then simulate six- and eight-sided dice.
rows.evidence: DiceLab checks; interval argument; documented parameter/return types.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish L06 Rolling Dice; label the four outputs and total.

rows.task: Use the provided complete Player class in AliasingLab. Create two objects, call instance methods and diagram reassignment, aliasing and null. Discuss signatures without requiring class design yet.
rows.evidence: Four-stage reference diagram; AliasingLab checks; distinguish class and instance calls.
rows.homework: 20 min: trace the first three-object diagram in L13; do not type the full legacy project.

rows.task: Complete String Activity with short teacher-supplied strings. Draw indexes; implement firstWord and safeSlice from supplied headers, then check boundary behavior.
rows.evidence: WordTools checks; index diagram; predicted length/substring/indexOf results.
rows.homework: 20 min: L05 Working with Strings prediction/verification table; six JQR method cards.

rows.task: Predict the Lineup outputs. Repair sameText and order; compare ==, equals and compareTo using distinct String objects. Keep split/parsing for Unit 4.
rows.evidence: StringRelations checks; corrected Lineup answers; explain immutability.
rows.homework: 20 min: retry three missed String outputs and finish method cards.

rows.task: Predict the six Unit1Review results before running. Repair the two weakest categories, then complete eight teacher-selected AP Classroom Unit 1 questions.
rows.evidence: Review checks; eight MC responses; personal two-item error log.
rows.homework: 25 min: rehearse casts, method calls and String indexes; rewrite two corrected examples.

rows.task: Complete 12 current-topic MC questions (26 min), two short supplied-header code tasks (24 min), then explain and begin corrections (25 min).
rows.evidence: Independent assessment and first corrections; no compiler during assessment.
rows.homework: 15 min: finish corrections and make a boundary-test checklist.

rows.task: Translate temperature rules into a cascading if/else. Test 39/40, 59/60 and 79/80 before running; explain equality and branch order.
rows.evidence: Working activities program and six-case boundary table.
rows.homework: 20 min: Date Validation month/year conditions and expected outcomes, before coding.

rows.task: Implement the date checks. Build a truth table for a compound condition, negate it with De Morgan and compare both versions; use short-circuit guards.
rows.evidence: Validated program; leap-year/boundary tests; equivalent-condition proof.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish Date Validation tests and repair one compound Boolean expression.

rows.task: Trace initialization, test, body and update. Complete sumTo and countBy in LoopTrace; compare zero/one/many iterations. Record the final trace row for countBy(1, 8, 2).
rows.evidence: LoopTrace checks; trace table; a termination explanation.
rows.homework: Up to 20 min by Oct 20: finish the loop trace repair before or after the school trip week. No required work during Oct 12-16.

rows.task: No AP CSA meeting. School grade-level programs.
rows.evidence: No submission.
rows.homework: None.

rows.task: Write Powers of 2 without Math.pow. Complete Loop Programs #1 items 1, 2 and 4. Compare a running sum with repeated multiplication.
rows.evidence: Four short programs; loop bounds and accumulator explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: L10 temperature extrema with all-negative and tied values; finish in class next time if needed.

rows.task: Finish a short extrema check. Implement removeCharacter and countDouble; count non-overlapping pairs, including the aaaa case. Trace an empty and one-character String.
rows.evidence: StringAlgorithms checks; one original edge case; precise loop invariant.
rows.homework: 20 min: complete countLetter/removeLetter in W09 as transfer, using the supplied headers.

rows.task: Implement the staircase; trace factor-pair loops. Count body executions for n=3 and n=5 and compare constant, linear and quadratic growth.
rows.evidence: PatternLab checks; two operation-count tables and a growth explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish W20 runtime counts and one wrong-bound correction.

rows.task: Attempt 2024 Q1 Feeder part (a) independently for 20 minutes. Compare to the specification; discuss repeated calls in part (b), then revise.
rows.evidence: Timed method, annotated correction and normal/boundary tests.
rows.homework: 20 min: implement the corrected method in a small runner with fixed test inputs.

rows.task: Finish the Feeder runner; choose the weakest of loop bounds, String scans or Boolean equivalence for focused repair. Explain a method without executing it.
rows.evidence: Working runner; six mixed retrieval answers; one oral explanation.
rows.homework: 25 min: revise the Unit 2 error log and rehearse two method skeletons.

rows.task: Complete 12 MC questions (26 min), two short methods covering loops and Strings (34 min), and an explanation/correction (15 min).
rows.evidence: Independent assessment; one corrected loop invariant.
rows.homework: 15 min: complete corrections and sketch fields/behaviors for a Duck.

rows.task: Turn the Duck diagram into private fields and a public interface. Design BandBooster; discuss which information the model needs and how design can exclude users.
rows.evidence: Class diagram; BandBooster field/constructor skeleton; one design-impact paragraph.
rows.homework: 20 min: implement BandBooster constructor and getName.

rows.task: Finish updateSales and a small runner with three fictional boosters. Test state before and after repeated updates; distinguish a returned value from printed output.
rows.evidence: Working BandBooster class/runner; at least four predicted/actual tests.
rows.homework: 20 min: write a second constructor proposal with explicit defaults; explain valid initialization.

rows.task: Trace mutation versus reassignment in Changing People, then complete the corresponding reference-ownership project. Explain passing a reference by value.
rows.evidence: Before/after object diagrams; reference-ownership checks; a method contract.
rows.homework: 20 min: trace two aliases to one object and one reassigned parameter.

rows.task: Complete Ticket and observe what all objects share. Link the model to Counting Transactions; decide which members belong to the class and which belong to each object.
rows.evidence: Ticket checks; two-object trace; static-versus-instance explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: complete W31 static-access questions and repair one illegal call.

rows.task: Complete HotelRoom; repair shadowed fields with this, reason about private/public access, and explain a precondition at a code conference.
rows.evidence: HotelRoom checks; scope map; correct constructor assignments.
rows.homework: None over Thanksgiving. Keep your class-design checklist for Nov 30.

rows.task: Re-entry trace, then write StepTracker from its interaction table. Test no recorded days, below threshold, exactly threshold and repeated updates.
rows.evidence: StepTracker.java plus table-driven tests; explain averageSteps numeric type.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish tests and annotate field choices.

rows.task: Finish StepTracker, swap test cases, and do eight Unit 3 MC questions. Explain a complete constructor and a state-changing method without the IDE.
rows.evidence: Final StepTracker; eight responses; revised class-design checklist.
rows.homework: 20 min: rehearse a fresh class specification; no additional project.

rows.task: Write 2026 Q2 Bottle independently (35 min), answer eight selected Unit 3 MC items (17 min), then inspect examples and start corrections (23 min).
rows.evidence: Complete independent class, MC responses and correction notes.
rows.homework: 15 min: finish corrections.

rows.task: Compare two non-personal datasets. Identify a question, source, units, missing-data risk and collection bias. Run DataConsent/DatasetFit examples and write a data-use note.
rows.evidence: One-page dataset brief; one defensible and one unsupported claim; checks for selected starter tasks.
rows.homework: 20 min: inspect a small teacher-provided public weather sample and label fields/units.

rows.task: Create primitive and object arrays; distinguish length from valid indexes and default values. Complete ArrayAccess and begin a single-pass sales traversal.
rows.evidence: ArrayAccess checks; reference/default-value diagram; predicted totals.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish the sales total/average with supplied fictional data.

rows.task: Build count/sum/min/max passes. Show why assigning an enhanced-for loop variable does not replace an array element; contrast object mutation.
rows.evidence: Traversal checks; corrected enhanced-for examples; bounds explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: trace reversal on even- and odd-length arrays; write swaps before coding.

rows.task: Finish the array toolkit, then reverse actual elements in place. Test empty, one-element, odd and even lengths. Explain copying versus aliasing.
rows.evidence: Array algorithm checks; reverse method; four test cases.
rows.homework: None over winter break. Save the array summary and expected outputs for Jan 6.

rows.task: Re-entry array trace. Open a File with Scanner, read tokens with hasNext/nextInt, and explain imports, file location, close and the required exception declaration.
rows.evidence: TokenReader checks; annotated read loop; source file packaged with code.
rows.homework: 20 min: trace Inventory Auditor on the seven values in L21; predict sum/minimum.

rows.task: Complete InventoryAudit using the supplied synthetic data. Compare token reading with line reading; test whitespace variation and document empty-file behavior.
rows.evidence: InventoryAudit checks; sum/minimum result; empty-file rule and working-directory note.
rows.homework: 20 min: preview Weather Data Analyzer and mark where each weekly line begins/ends.

rows.task: Use the corrected W46 project. Process each weekly line; split values and parse numeric Strings. Compute each weekly mean and overall maximum.
rows.evidence: WeatherData checks; per-week results; a token/line trace and parsing explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish the three-week fixture and a one-week test.

rows.task: Apply the same pipeline to the selected public weather sample. Calculate an aggregate, identify a limitation and verify one result by hand.
rows.evidence: Source-cited data brief, program, two checks and a supported conclusion.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish the brief and note one missing-value assumption.

rows.task: Contrast int with Integer, parse methods, boxing/unboxing and null. Complete ListMethods with typed ArrayList<Integer> and ArrayList<String>.
rows.evidence: Wrapper/list method checks; table of add/get/set/remove/size effects and return values.
rows.homework: 20 min: make method cards and predict a six-operation list trace.

rows.task: Complete ten MC questions (22 min) and a file-to-array method task (25 min), then explain and repair errors (28 min).
rows.evidence: Independent checkpoint; corrected file loop and wrapper/list trace.
rows.homework: 15 min: finish corrections.

rows.task: Complete ListTraversal, then use ListRemoval to expose skipped adjacent matches. Trace forward, adjusted-forward and backward passes before coding.
rows.evidence: List traversal/removal checks; before/after index table.
rows.homework: 20 min: test adjacent removals, all removed and none removed.

rows.task: Create ArrayList<Item>, instantiate Item objects and compute quantity-weighted totals. Start with three fixed products; add interactive input only after the core works.
rows.evidence: Typed cart with correct total and getPrice/getQuantity calls; fixed test basket.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish one receipt test, including quantity greater than one.

rows.task: Add a remove-matching-items method as a plan-authored extension. Test consecutive matches and an empty cart; explain mutation order and present the design.
rows.evidence: Final cart files, three mutation tests and a short code conference.
rows.homework: 20 min: write the removal algorithm from memory, then correct it.

rows.task: Attempt the one-method Attendance problem for 23 minutes. Trace matches across both lists and verify that neither list changes, then revise and test.
rows.evidence: Timed method; corrected method; cases for matching and nonmatching IDs.
rows.homework: 20 min: explain nested-list traversal and one missed case.

rows.task: Map Processing x/y to row/column, create a rectangular grid and trace dimensions. Use a 2-by-3 array to expose swapped bounds.
rows.evidence: GridBridge checks; labeled row/column diagram; correct dimension expressions.
rows.homework: 20 min: predict two row-major and two column-major traversals.

rows.task: Traverse a nonsquare grid in both orders, then implement row sums, column sums and a search with early return. Explain every loop bound.
rows.evidence: GridTraversal/GridAlgorithms checks for selected methods; 2-by-3 test grid.
rows.homework: 20 min: hand-compute row, column and diagonal totals for a 3-by-3 square.

rows.task: Build row/column/diagonal sum helpers and compare them with the first-row total. Use the supplied magic-square context and a deliberately broken square.
rows.evidence: Core checker; two expected-result grids; bounds explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: add one grid that has equal rows but unequal columns.

rows.task: Finish tests and demonstrate the checker. Explain why changing cells while scanning can invalidate a decision; trace a separate read/write grid example.
rows.evidence: Final checker, four tests and one original debugging explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: rewrite one row/column method without compiler feedback.

rows.task: Attempt getPointsForRow for 23 minutes. Trace sums and same-color comparison, then test all-same and mixed-color rows and revise.
rows.evidence: Timed method, correction and two concrete test rows.
rows.homework: 20 min: describe a linear search and its result when a target is absent.

rows.task: Implement/trace sequential search over integers and Strings. Test first, last, missing and duplicated targets; explain the returned index contract.
rows.evidence: SearchLab checks for linear cases; comparison-count table.
rows.homework: 20 min: trace searches in a sorted seven-element array and record low/high/mid.

rows.task: Trace iterative binary search and its sorted-input precondition. Compare comparisons with linear search; test missing and boundary targets.
rows.evidence: Low/high/mid trace table; sorted-input counterexample; selected SearchLab checks.
rows.homework: 20 min: predict two selection-sort passes on five values.

rows.task: Use SortTrace to track selection-sort passes and insertion-sort shifts. State what prefix is settled/sorted and compare already-sorted/reversed inputs.
rows.evidence: SortTrace checks; one pass table for each algorithm; invariant explanation.
rows.homework: 20 min: complete one fresh trace of each sort; record comparisons versus swaps/shifts.

rows.task: Predict supplied methods before running RecursionTrace. Track separate local variables, base cases and output before/after each call.
rows.evidence: Call-stack diagrams and predicted output; RecursionTrace checks.
rows.homework: 20 min: four teacher-selected output traces from the recursion packet.

rows.assignment: Recursive binary search and merge sort
rows.task: Trace a recursive String/collection walk, binary search calls, and merge-sort split/merge stages. Explain the sorted halves before each merge.
rows.evidence: RecursiveAlgorithms checks; call trace; complete merge tree for eight values.
rows.homework: 20 min: one fresh recursive trace and one merge-stage explanation.

rows.task: Complete 12 analysis questions (26 min), a short 2D method (24 min), then correct the two weakest categories (25 min).
rows.evidence: Independent checkpoint; repaired 2D method and one trace.
rows.homework: 15 min: finish two corrections.

rows.task: Finish authentic-data transfer if pending. Choose array, ArrayList or 2D array for a justified analysis; implement one aggregate and one filter/group comparison.
rows.evidence: Source-cited investigation, justified structure choice and two manual checks.
rows.homework: 20 min: finalize the investigation and a five-sentence limitation statement.

rows.task: Complete 18 MC questions (39 min), one new ArrayList or 2D method (26 min), and a reflection (10 min). Earlier checkpoints provide evidence for the other structure.
rows.evidence: Independent assessment with all Unit 4 strands represented across the assessment cycle.
rows.homework: 20 min: complete two corrections with counterexamples.

rows.task: Conference on the assessment. Repair the two weakest collection algorithms, explain data-file assumptions and retry a fresh search/sort/recursion trace.
rows.evidence: Corrected code; two fresh successful traces; April priority list.
rows.homework: 20 min: rehearse one ArrayList and one 2D pattern.

rows.task: Complete 21 fresh MC items in 45 minutes. Spend 30 minutes classifying errors by topic and choosing two April priorities.
rows.evidence: Baseline responses; correction plan; list of uncertain Java behaviors.
rows.homework: Optional, at most 40 min over spring break: redo four misses and one short method. No new content or required break packet.

rows.assignment: Return from break and diagnostic repair
rows.task: Retrieve String/index/list patterns, correct the baseline and do one targeted method. This is the first recovery slot if core content needs one more lesson.
rows.evidence: Updated error log; corrected method; two named review priorities.
rows.homework: 20 min: trace a String scan and annotate a method specification.

rows.task: Attempt 2026 Q1 Account in 28 minutes, covering both constructor and String method. Use remaining time to compare to the contract, correct and test.
rows.evidence: Timed Q1; two corrected parts; explain unchanged username postcondition.
rows.homework: 20 min: rewrite the weakest part from a blank editor.

rows.task: Attempt 2025 Q2 as a fresh class task (25 min). Compare the representation and method logic to Bottle and StepTracker; correct and explain.
rows.evidence: Timed class; field/state diagram; corrected method.
rows.homework: 20 min: one constructor/state-change trace and a short class checklist.

rows.task: Attempt 2024 Q3 parts (a)/(b) as a selected skill set (30 min), then identify list iteration, adjacent-element and String assumptions and revise.
rows.evidence: Timed list/String methods; corrected tests for adjacent entries.
rows.homework: 20 min: redo one list algorithm independently.

rows.task: Attempt 2024 Q4 GridPath part (a) (23 min) and trace part (b). Correct bounds and helper-method calls. If absent for senior retreat, use Apr 22.
rows.evidence: Timed 2D method and corrected row/column trace.
rows.homework: 15 min: revise the two most common 2D errors.
rows.calendar_note: If you are away on the senior retreat, complete this review during the April 22 recovery lesson.

rows.homework: 20 min: correct one unfinished response and record a pacing adjustment.

rows.evidence: Eight justified answers; one corrected independent method or trace.

rows.evidence: Timed half-section responses; error categories and time per question.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish the correction log; no new full packet.

rows.evidence: Second half-section responses; combined 42-question analysis.

rows.task: Use a fresh current-format Methods/Control and Class Design pair for 50 minutes, then debrief for 25 minutes.
rows.evidence: Two independent FRQs and focused correction notes.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish one correction; keep the remaining pair unseen.

rows.task: Use a fresh current-format ArrayList and 2D pair for 40 minutes, then review both simulations for 35 minutes.
rows.evidence: Two independent FRQs; combined four-question skill review.
rows.homework: 15 min: revise the personal reference/error checklist.

rows.task: Open the official preview, locate the JQR and practice entering/indenting Java. Complete one short plain-editor method and one targeted trace without compiler feedback.
rows.evidence: Preview/navigation completed; typed method; final two-error repair.
rows.homework: 15 min: confirm coordinator instructions, device readiness and permitted materials.

rows.task: Complete six familiar retrieval items, walk through a class/list/grid plan, and confirm when and where to report. End with time for questions.
rows.evidence: Personal one-page checklist and confirmed reporting details.
rows.homework: No new work; follow coordinator directions for May 12.

rows.evidence: Exam only.
rows.homework: None.

rows.task: Reflect on preparation, then choose a weather-data tool, Shopping Cart extension or grid simulation. Define a user, a question and a smallest working version.
rows.evidence: Half-page proposal with three success criteria.
rows.homework: 20 min: refine the proposal and a sketch of the interface/model.

rows.task: Specify classes, data structure, input/output and three acceptance tests. Build a skeleton and agree on two implementation milestones.
rows.evidence: Design diagram, acceptance tests and runnable skeleton.
rows.homework: 20 min: implement the smallest core method.

rows.task: Implement one complete input-to-output path. Test it with a tiny fixture and explain a design decision in a code conference.
rows.evidence: Runnable first version and one passing acceptance test.
rows.homework: 25 min: finish the core feature and record the next bug.

rows.task: Complete required features and run peer-created boundary tests. Prioritize correctness over adding features.
rows.evidence: All required features working; bug list with reproduction steps.
rows.homework: 20 min: repair the highest-priority bug.

rows.task: Resolve bugs, test from a clean launch and write README instructions, data attribution and limitations. Rehearse a five-minute demo.
rows.evidence: Candidate final ZIP/project folder, README and test evidence.
rows.homework: 20 min: finish demo preparation and documentation.

rows.task: Each student demonstrates the project, explains a core method and handles one new test case. Use remaining time for revisions.
rows.evidence: Project demo, explanation and final revision list.
rows.homework: 15 min: final edits and a short learning reflection.

rows.task: Submit the final project and choose three artifacts showing growth in code analysis, class design and data processing. Reflect on one repaired misconception.
rows.evidence: Private portfolio/project ZIP, reflection and final test evidence.
rows.homework: None; follow school instructions if an additional final-exam meeting is required.
